jb.definition: sand = JB 1-4, clay = JB 5-8, humus = JB 11; shares are of the JB-mapped area (farmland map, not all land)
jb.ranking_rule: only municipalities with at least 50 km2 of JB-mapped area (75 of 99 qualify); the rest are small or built-up and the JB map covers little of them

geology.note: share_of_land = of all land; share_of_mapped = of the area GEUS maps to a sediment family (the rest is water, built-up, fill)

peat.comparison_note: The Danish peat layer maps lowland soils with more than 6 % organic carbon; GEUS maps surface sediment type, 'peat and gyttja', which includes thin or lean peat. They are different things, so GEUS is shown only as a cross-check (for example Bornholm has almost none in the Danish layer).

nitrogen_retention.note: share of land area; 'not mapped' is land with no retention polygon

organic_nitrogen.note: Interval as given in the Landbrugsstyrelsen layer; the file does not state a unit. 0 = category 1 (value 0)

sightings.definition: records from GBIF, country DK, with coordinates, license CC0 or CC BY, coordinate uncertainty <= 2 km. 'On land' = inside a municipality polygon.

earthworm_headline.square_definition: 10 x 10 km squares with at least 50 km2 of land (mostly land); counting every square that touches land gives 8.5 % of 639 squares

sightings.sightings_note: Group list is whatever is in raw/gbif at run time. Counts are record rows (one row per GBIF occurrence), not individuals. 10 km squares are aligned to multiples of 10 km in EPSG:25832.

ph_check.method: SoilGrids 2.0 pH(H2O) at 250 m, depth-weighted mean of 0-5, 5-15 and 15-30 cm (the 0-30 cm plough layer), and the 0-5 cm layer. 'cropland' = ESA WorldCover class 40 at 100 m, each 100 m cell takes the value of the 250 m SoilGrids cell it sits in. 'all land' = every 250 m cell whose centre is inside a municipality.

meta.grid: EPSG:25832, 25 m cells; land = cells whose centre is inside a municipality polygon (Eurostat GISCO LAU 2021)
meta.region_rule: North Jutland = Region Nordjylland. West/East Jutland split by the Main Stationary Line (Hovedopholdslinjen): a municipality is West when its administrative centre lies west or south of the line, East otherwise. Samsø is counted with Zealand, Christiansø with Bornholm, Læsø with North Jutland.
meta.region_caveat: No line file was available. Eleven municipalities close to the line (see region_sensitivity) may straddle it; West Jutland barely changes without them but East Jutland's JB sand share falls from about 52 % to 36 %, so East Jutland's sand/clay split depends on where the line is drawn.
